# cssig

**Composite selection signals (CSS) for detecting signatures of
selection.**

An R implementation of the CSS method of Randhawa, Khatkar, Thomson and
Raadsma.

``` r

# install
remotes::install_github("msk99/cssig")                    # add build_vignettes = TRUE for vignettes

# run on the bundled example data
library(cssig)
data(css_sim_small)

x   <- css_input(css_sim_small, tests = c(fst = "high", xpehh = "high", ddaf = "high"))
res <- css(x) |> css_smooth() |> css_threshold(top = 0.001)
reg <- css_regions(res)

summary(reg)
css_manhattan(res, regions = reg)

# help
?css
vignette("cssig")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What this package is

Genome scans for selection rely on statistics like *F*_(ST), XP-EHH and
ΔDAF. Each is sensitive to a different aspect of a selective sweep, and
none is decisive on its own — run three tests on the same data and you
typically get three partly overlapping answers.

CSS combines them into a single non-parametric index. Each constituent
test is ranked genome-wide, the ranks become normal quantiles, and the
quantiles are averaged at every SNP. A locus where several tests agree
is amplified; a locus where only one test is extreme is pulled back
toward the genome-wide average.

**`cssig` takes pre-computed constituent statistics and does everything
downstream of them**: the CSS statistic, sliding-window smoothing,
empirical thresholds, region calling, FDR, reciprocal (signed) cohort
contrasts, and plots.

### The method

For test *i* at SNP *j*, with *m* tests and *n* SNPs:

| Step | Operation         |                                       |
|------|-------------------|---------------------------------------|
| 1    | rank genome-wide  | `R[j,i] = rank(T[,i])`                |
| 2    | fractional rank   | `R'[j,i] = R[j,i] / (n + 1)`          |
| 3    | normal quantile   | `Z[j,i] = qnorm(R'[j,i])`             |
| 4    | mean across tests | `Zbar[j] = mean(Z[j,])`               |
| 5    | p-value           | `p[j] = 1 - pnorm(sqrt(m) * Zbar[j])` |
| 6    | CSS               | `-log10(p[j])`                        |

### Scope

**In scope** — the CSS statistic and everything after it, plus the
constituents that are one-liners from allele frequencies
([`css_fst()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fst.md),
[`css_ddaf()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_ddaf.md),
[`css_dsaf()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_dsaf.md)).

**Out of scope** — VCF/PLINK parsing, phasing, imputation, and XP-EHH
computation. Use [rehh](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rehh),
[selscan](https://github.com/szpiech/selscan) or hapbin for haplotype
statistics and bring the output here;
[`read_rehh_xpehh()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/read_rehh_xpehh.md)
and
[`read_selscan_xpehh()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/read_selscan_xpehh.md)
handle the coercion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

Requires **R \>= 4.1**, and `remotes` for the install command at the top
of this page.

`install_github()` skips vignettes by default, which is why
[`vignette("cssig")`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/articles/cssig.md)
can report “not found” — add `build_vignettes = TRUE` (it needs `knitr`
and `rmarkdown`). Both vignettes are also readable on GitHub without
installing:
[cssig.Rmd](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/vignettes/cssig.Rmd) and
[simulation.Rmd](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/vignettes/simulation.Rmd).

Or from a local source tree:

``` bash
git clone https://github.com/msk99/cssig.git
R CMD INSTALL cssig
```

Hard dependencies are only `data.table` (\>= 1.15) and `ggplot2`.
Optional extras, each needed for one feature:

``` r

install.packages(c("fdrtool",  # css_fdr(method = "fdrtool" / "isotonic")
                   "circlize", # css_circos()
                   "rehh"))    # computing XP-EHH in the first place
```

`scrm` and `rehh` are additionally needed only to *regenerate* the
bundled example data from `data-raw/`; they are never loaded by the
installed package.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Usage

### 1. Prepare the input

You need one row per SNP: a chromosome, a position, and one numeric
column per constituent test.

``` r

head(css_sim_small[, .(chr, pos, fst, xpehh, ddaf)])
```

[`css_input()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_input.md)
validates it and records, per test, which direction means *more evidence
of selection*:

``` r

x <- css_input(my_stats,
               chr = "chr", pos = "pos", snp = "rsid",
               tests = c(fst = "high", xpehh = "high", ddaf = "high"))
```

| `direction` | Meaning | Typical use |
|----|----|----|
| `"high"` | use as-is | *F*_(ST); XP-EHH with the selected population as target; ΔDAF as selected − reference |
| `"low"` | negate before ranking | Tajima’s D, π ratios |
| `"abs"` | use magnitude only | a signed test whose sign you do not trust |

It accepts a `data.frame`, `tibble`, `data.table` or matrix, and returns
a `data.table` keyed on `(chr, pos)`.

Two details that surprise people:

- **`chr` comes back as a factor**, not character. That is deliberate:
  as character, a keyed table sorts `1, 10, 2, 22, X`, which would
  scramble the Manhattan axis and the order of called regions. The
  factor carries genomic order, so you get `1, 2, 10, 22, X`. Filtering
  is unaffected — both `chr == "2"` and `chr == 2` work.
- **A column named `snp` is picked up automatically.** Pass
  `snp = "rsid"` for a differently named one; with neither, identifiers
  of the form `"chr:pos"` are generated.

**If your tests come from different tools** — and so cover slightly
different SNP sets — join them explicitly rather than hoping they line
up:

``` r

a <- data.frame(chr = 1, pos = c(100, 200, 300), fst   = c(0.10, 0.22, 0.31))
b <- data.frame(chr = 1, pos = c(200, 300, 400), xpehh = c(1.1, 2.2, 0.4))

css_merge_tests(fst = a, xpehh = b, all = FALSE)   # FALSE = complete cases only
#> Merged 2 tests on (chr, pos), keeping the intersection: 2 SNPs.
#>   fst                3 in ->       2 retained (66.7%)
#>   xpehh              3 in ->       2 retained (66.7%)
#>       chr   pos   fst xpehh
#>    <char> <num> <num> <num>
#> 1:      1   200  0.22   1.1
#> 2:      1   300  0.31   2.2
```

Use `all = TRUE` to keep the union instead, leaving `NA` where a test is
missing. The retention report exists because silent SNP loss at this
step is the commonest way a scan goes quietly wrong.

### 2. Getting the constituent statistics

From allele counts and frequencies, in-package:

``` r

fst  <- css_fst(count1 = derived_selected, n1 = n_ind_selected,
                count2 = derived_reference, n2 = n_ind_reference)
ddaf <- css_ddaf(daf_selected, daf_reference)   # needs ancestral allele
dsaf <- css_dsaf(freq_selected, freq_reference) # ancestral-free alternative
```

XP-EHH needs phased haplotypes, so it comes from elsewhere:

``` r

# rehh
sel <- rehh::scan_hh(hh_selected);  ref <- rehh::scan_hh(hh_reference)
xp  <- read_rehh_xpehh(rehh::ies2xpehh(sel, ref))

# selscan
xp  <- read_selscan_xpehh("chr1.xpehh.out", chr = 1)
```

### 3. Run the pipeline

``` r

res <- css(x)                                          # the CSS statistic
res <- css_smooth(res, half_width = 5e5, min_snps = 5) # 1 Mb sliding window
res <- css_threshold(res, top = 0.001)                 # empirical top 0.1%
```

Useful arguments:

| Function | Argument | Default | Notes |
|----|----|----|----|
| [`css()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css.md) | `ties` | `"average"` | passed to [`data.table::frank()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/data.table/man/frank.html) |
|  | `na_action` | `"pairwise"` | uses each SNP’s own *m*; `"omit"` for strict complete cases |
|  | `weights` | `NULL` | equal weights = the published method |
| [`css_smooth()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_smooth.md) | `half_width` | `5e5` | half-width in bp, so 1 Mb total |
|  | `min_snps` | `5` | sparser windows are masked |
|  | `cols` | `NULL` | also smooth the constituent tests, for comparison plots |
| [`css_threshold()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_threshold.md) | `top` | `0.001` | top 0.1%, as in both papers |
|  | `top2` | `0.01` | the more permissive tier used by `method = "flank"` |

### 4. Call regions

Two published rules, one from each paper:

``` r

css_regions(res, method = "cluster")  # 2014: >= 3 significant SNPs in a window
css_regions(res, method = "flank")    # 2015: 1 top-0.1% SNP + >= 5 top-1% neighbours
```

Both return one row per region with the span, peak SNP, and — when the
constituent tests are still attached — how many SNPs in each test’s
*own* top fraction fall inside. That last part is how you tell a signal
supported by several tests from one driven by a single test.

`start_padded` / `end_padded` carry the ±0.5 Mb both papers add for gene
mining. The padding is never folded into `start` / `end`, so region
boundaries are not silently inflated.

### 5. FDR

``` r

res <- css_fdr(res, method = "BH")        # default, no extra dependency
res <- css_fdr(res, method = "fdrtool")   # the route used in the 2014 paper
```

Run this **before**
[`css_smooth()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_smooth.md).
Smoothing averages −log10(*p*) over neighbouring SNPs, and the result is
no longer a p-value;
[`css_fdr()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fdr.md)
refuses smoothed input rather than returning numbers that look like
q-values but are not. See the caveat in *Things worth knowing* below.

### 6. Reciprocal (signed) analysis

The 2015 paper compares two cohorts in both directions, so a signal’s
sign says which cohort carries it:

``` r

fwd <- css_input(dat,      tests = c(fst = "high", xpehh = "high", ddaf = "high"))
rev <- css_input(dat_swapped, tests = c(fst = "high", xpehh = "high", ddaf = "high"))
recip <- css_reciprocal(fwd, rev, labels = c("large", "small"))
css_manhattan_mirror(recip)
```

### 7. Weighting the constituents

Off by default, because equal weights are the published method. Use it
when you have a stated reason to trust one test less — not by tuning
until the answer improves:

``` r

res <- css(x, weights = c(fst = 1, xpehh = 1, ddaf = 0.25))
```

`weights = c(1,1,1)` reproduces the unweighted statistic exactly, and
[`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) flags a weighted run.
Worked example with known truth in
[`vignette("simulation")`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/articles/simulation.md).

### 8. Plots

Every plot function returns a `ggplot` object you can modify, except
[`css_circos()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_circos.md),
which draws with `circlize`.

| Function | What it shows |
|----|----|
| [`css_manhattan()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_manhattan.md) | genome-wide CSS, alternating chromosomes, threshold line |
| [`css_manhattan_mirror()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_manhattan_mirror.md) | two reciprocal directions above and below zero |
| [`css_chrom_plot()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_chrom_plot.md) | one chromosome: raw points, smoothed line, gene marks |
| [`css_region_plot()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_region_plot.md) | one region, faceted into CSS + each constituent test |
| [`css_qq()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_qq.md), [`css_pdist()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_pdist.md) | p-value calibration |
| [`css_fdr_density()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fdr_density.md) | q-values inside called regions vs the rest of the genome |
| [`css_test_cor()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_test_cor.md) | correlation among constituents and CSS |
| [`css_circos()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_circos.md) | circular multi-track genome plot |
| [`css_theme()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_theme.md), [`css_genome_coords()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_genome_coords.md) | building blocks for custom plots |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Things worth knowing

**CSS depends only on ranks.** Standardising XP-EHH or ΔDAF to *N*(0,1),
as both papers do, leaves CSS *exactly* unchanged — it matters only for
plotting. Any strictly increasing transform of a constituent gives
identical CSS.

**Ranks are genome-wide.** Adding or removing SNPs changes every SNP’s
score, so keep the SNP set fixed when comparing runs.

**The CSS p-value is not calibrated on real data.** The formula assumes
the constituent tests are independent. They are not, and the correlation
is not always positive: in the bundled `css_sim`, XP-EHH and ΔDAF
correlate at about −0.32, which *deflates* the variance of Zbar
(observed sd 0.90 rather than 1.00; permuting each test restores it to
1.00). Treat CSS as a **ranking**, not a tail probability. This is why
both papers threshold on the empirical top 0.1% rather than on a
p-value, and why q-values deserve a look at
[`css_qq()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_qq.md) first.

**Pipeline stages modify their object by reference.** `data.table`
semantics, so a multi-million-row table is never copied between stages:

``` r

res <- css(x)
"css" %in% names(x)   # TRUE -- x and res are the same object
```

Your original input is always safe —
[`css_input()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_input.md)
copies it once on the way in — but if you want each stage to return a
fresh copy, pass `.copy = TRUE`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Bundled data

Simulated, and generated the slow way: a population is simulated and the
statistics are computed from it, rather than the statistics being drawn
from a distribution. That matters because the three tests are correlated
through a shared genealogy, and inventing that correlation would make
any demonstration circular.

| Object | Contents |
|----|----|
| `css_sim` | 46,976 SNPs × 29 bovine autosomes, 8 vs 8 breeds, 800 animals |
| `css_sim_small` | 5,502 SNPs on chromosomes 1–2, for fast examples |
| `css_sim_truth` | the 7 known signatures: 6 sweeps and one deliberate false positive |

**These data are simulated and describe no real animal, breed or
genome.** The generating scripts are in `data-raw/`; see
[`?css_sim`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_sim.md).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Documentation

``` r

vignette("cssig")       # getting started
vignette("simulation")  # how the data were built, CSS vs its constituents,
                        # the weights demo, and where the method fails
?css                    # the statistic, and the two documented deviations
?css_fdr                # calibration caveats in full
```

## Repository contents

| Path | What it is |
|----|----|
| `R/`, `man/`, `tests/`, `vignettes/` | the package |
| `data/` | the simulated example datasets |
| `data-raw/` | scripts that regenerate them ([design notes](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/data-raw/README.md)) |
| `inst/extdata/` | a small selscan fixture used by the reader examples |

`data-raw/` and the pkgdown/CI configuration are excluded from the built
package via `.Rbuildignore`, so the installed package carries only the
code, data, documentation and tests.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Troubleshooting

**[`vignette("cssig")`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/articles/cssig.md)
says “not found”.** `install_github()` does not build vignettes unless
asked. Reinstall with `build_vignettes = TRUE` (see
[Installation](#installation)), or read them on GitHub.

**Plots crash R, or fail with `no applicable method for 'depth'`, on
macOS.** Symptoms are a session killed by `zsh: trace trap`, or an error
followed by `can't shut down a locked device`. Once it happens the
graphics device is wedged and every later plot fails, so **restart R
first**.

Then work out which of two situations you are in:

``` r

plot(1:10)                                                  # base graphics
print(ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point())
```

- **Those also fail** — R’s on-screen Quartz device is at fault, not
  this package. A macOS crash report will show `CFRelease` inside
  `-[QuartzCocoaView drawRect:]` with no package code on the stack.
  Write plots to files instead, or use RStudio or Positron, which use a
  different device.
- **Those succeed but a `cssig` plot still fails** — that is a bug here;
  please [open an issue](https://github.com/msk99/cssig/issues) with
  your [`sessionInfo()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/sessionInfo.html).
  Version 1.0.0 removed the infinite rectangle bounds that were the
  likeliest trigger, so make sure you are current.

Either way, writing to a file is a reliable workaround:

``` r

ggplot2::ggsave("manhattan.png", css_manhattan(res, regions = reg),
                width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 150)
```

# Package index

## Input

Getting constituent statistics into shape

- [`css_input()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_input.md)
  : Assemble constituent selection statistics for a CSS analysis
- [`css_merge_tests()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_merge_tests.md)
  : Join per-test statistic tables into a single CSS input
- [`read_selscan_xpehh()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/read_selscan_xpehh.md)
  : Read XP-EHH output from selscan
- [`read_rehh_xpehh()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/read_rehh_xpehh.md)
  : Coerce rehh XP-EHH output for use with CSS

## The CSS pipeline

Score, smooth, threshold, call regions, estimate FDR

- [`css()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css.md) : Compute
  composite selection signals
- [`css_smooth()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_smooth.md)
  : Smooth CSS scores in sliding genomic windows
- [`css_threshold()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_threshold.md)
  : Apply an empirical significance threshold to CSS scores
- [`css_regions()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_regions.md)
  : Call genomic regions under selection
- [`css_fdr()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fdr.md) :
  Estimate false discovery rates for CSS p-values
- [`css_reciprocal()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_reciprocal.md)
  : Reciprocal (signed) composite selection signals

## Constituent statistics

Helpers for the constituents computable from allele frequencies

- [`css_fst()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fst.md) :
  Weir and Cockerham's F_ST between two cohorts
- [`css_ddaf()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_ddaf.md) :
  Change in derived allele frequency between cohorts
- [`css_dsaf()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_dsaf.md) :
  Change in selected allele frequency between cohorts
- [`css_standardize()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_standardize.md)
  : Standardise a statistic to mean zero and unit variance

## Visualisation

- [`css_manhattan()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_manhattan.md)
  : Genome-wide Manhattan plot of composite selection signals
- [`css_manhattan_mirror()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_manhattan_mirror.md)
  : Mirrored Manhattan plot for reciprocal cohort contrasts
- [`css_chrom_plot()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_chrom_plot.md)
  : Single-chromosome CSS plot
- [`css_region_plot()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_region_plot.md)
  : Regional plot with constituent test tracks
- [`css_qq()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_qq.md) : QQ
  plot of CSS p-values
- [`css_pdist()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_pdist.md)
  : Histogram of CSS p-values
- [`css_fdr_density()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_fdr_density.md)
  : Density of q-values inside called regions versus the rest of the
  genome
- [`css_test_cor()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_test_cor.md)
  : Correlation among constituent tests and CSS
- [`css_circos()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_circos.md)
  : Circular genome plot of CSS and its constituent tests
- [`css_theme()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_theme.md)
  : A minimal theme for CSS plots
- [`css_genome_coords()`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_genome_coords.md)
  : Build cumulative genome coordinates for a genome-wide plot

## Data

- [`css_sim`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_sim.md) :
  Simulated multi-breed cattle panel with known selection signatures
- [`css_sim_small`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_sim_small.md)
  : Two-chromosome subset of the simulated panel
- [`css_sim_truth`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/css_sim_truth.md)
  : Known selection signatures in the simulated panel

## Methods

- [`summary(`*`<css_result>`*`)`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/summary.css_result.md)
  : Summarise a CSS result
- [`summary(`*`<css_regions>`*`)`](https://msk99.github.io/cssig/reference/summary.css_regions.md)
  : Summarise called regions
